title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00484
what_is_it: FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification reporting a UFO/UAP encounter by a US Air Force F-35 fighter jet.
core_summary: On February 27, 2023, a USAF F-35 fighter jet (callsign BLOOD01) flying westbound at 12,500 feet reported both a sensor and visual detection of an unidentified object at its 2 o'clock position, approximately 68 nautical miles west-northwest of Luke Air Force Base near Glendale, Arizona. The object was traveling northeast-bound at flight level 185 (approximately 18,500 feet). The pilot could not identify the object, and the sighting was relayed by Albuquerque Air Route Traffic Control Center to FAA Operations.
interpretation_warnings: Single-source report from one aircrew; no corroborating radar data or additional witness accounts are included in this document.
The document is a preliminary operations center notification, not a completed investigation or case file.
No description of the object's shape, size, speed, or behavior beyond its heading and altitude is provided.
WOC reference number and initials (HM/BS) at the end likely refer to operations center staff but are not further identified.

public_headline: USAF F-35 pilot reported sensor and visual detection of unidentified object over Arizona
public_tldr: This FAA operations centre notification records a February 2023 incident in which a US Air Force F-35 fighter jet detected an unidentified object both on its sensors and visually while flying near Glendale, Arizona. The pilot could not identify the object, which was travelling in a different direction and at a higher altitude than the jet.
public_narrative:
This document is an FAA Washington Operations Center incident notification dated 27 February 2023. It is a preliminary internal report, not a completed investigation or case file. The notification was relayed by Albuquerque Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC), the air-traffic facility responsible for that airspace.

According to the report, a US Air Force F-35 fighter jet operating under the callsign BLOOD01 was flying westbound at 12,500 feet, approximately 68 nautical miles west-northwest of Luke Air Force Base near Glendale, Arizona. At 12:10 PM local time (MST), the pilot reported both a sensor hit and a visual sighting of an object at the aircraft's 2 o'clock position. The unidentified object was travelling northeast at flight level 185 — roughly 18,500 feet, some 6,000 feet above the F-35.

The pilot in command could not identify the object. The document provides no description of the object's shape, size, speed, or behaviour beyond its heading and altitude. There is no indication that the FAA or any other agency conducted a follow-up investigation based on this notification alone.

The report shows minimal redaction. It is a single-page operational log entry rather than a detailed analytical product. No radar data, photographs, or additional witness accounts are included.
public_caveats: This is a single-source report from one aircrew. No corroborating radar data or independent witness accounts are included in the document.
The document is a preliminary operations centre notification, not a completed investigation or final case file.
No description of the object's shape, size, speed, or behaviour is provided beyond its heading (northeast) and altitude (roughly 18,500 feet).
The report does not state any conclusion about what the object was. The pilot simply could not identify it.
There is little evidence of redaction, but the document's brevity means limited detail was recorded in the first place.
